item.title: Mini Crackme: check()
item.description:
Windows x64, rcx = pointer to a null-terminated ASCII string.
check: xor eax, eax ; acc = 0 xor edx, edx ; i = 0 .loop: movzx r8d, byte [rcx+rdx] test r8d, r8d jz .done add eax, r8d xor eax, edx ; mix in the loop index inc edx jmp .loop .done: cmp eax, 119h sete al ret
Find an ASCII string that makes check return true (al = 1).
Answer: CODE
Each iteration adds the byte at position i into eax, then XORs the running total with i itself (0, 1, 2, 3, ...) before advancing, so the accumulator is a sum interleaved with a position-dependent XOR mask, terminated by the usual test/jz on the null byte. Because XOR is its own inverse, you can solve backward from the target 0x119 (undo xor 3, subtract the last byte, undo xor 2, subtract, ...), or just verify forward: with 'C','O','D','E' (67, 79, 68, 69): 67 ->(+79=146)^1=147 ->(+68=215)^2=213 ->(+69=282)^3=281 = 0x119. Matches, so check("CODE") returns 1.
